rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The split sky marks the time of an event not ordinarily witnessed universally, though analogous signs occur in scattered worldly instances.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا مما لم تجر عادة بعمومه وإن استطرد بجريانه منه في أشياء منه في أماكن متفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky splits from the event’s awe and becomes openings through which angels and other signs descend.
rows.anchor: من هوله وعظمته فكانت أبوابا لنزول الملائكة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky becomes a bright red rose color because of the intense heat.
rows.anchor: أي حمراء مشرقة من شدة لهيبه

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī compares the color to a rose-colored horse: white tending toward red and yellow.
rows.anchor: كلون الفرس الورد وهو الأبيض الذي يضرب إلى حمرة وصفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image can mean something melted and clear like oil, or red leather, or a slippery place.
rows.anchor: ذائبة صافية كالشيء الذي يدهن به أو كالأديم الأحمر والمكان الزلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two twilight glows at sunrise and sunset provide a worldly sign resembling the described sky.
rows.anchor: وآية ذلك في الدنيا الشفقان عند الطلوع وعند الغروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause has an omitted answer, variously supplied as certain eyewitness knowledge, an exclamation at the horror, or a later event; omission magnifies the scene.
rows.anchor: وجواب { إذا } محذوف تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens’ preservation as a source of spirit, life, and provision is a great favor, while worldly signs already guide people to afterlife realities.
rows.anchor: ولما كان حفظ السماء عن مثل ذلك بتأخير إرسال هذا وغيره من الأسباب وجعلها محل الروح والحياة والرزق من أعظم الفواضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question addresses the two addressees’ denial of their Lord’s finely ordered care and the signs that substantiate the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي المربي لكما هذا التدبير المتقن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are not questioned to discover what they did; questioning is instead reproach, as in asking why they acted so.
rows.anchor: سؤال تعرف واستعلام بل سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ وكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eschatological day is long and has changing phases: in some periods people are questioned and in others they are not.
rows.anchor: ذلك اليوم طويل , وهو ذو ألوان تارة يسأل فيه وتارة لا يسأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 75:30 uses “that day” for the time when the soul reaches the collarbones, a period not bounded by ordinary night and day.
rows.anchor: أي يوم إذا بلغت الروح التراقي وهو لا يختص بليل ولا نهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction magnifies the matter and indicates that the sinner’s condition is publicly knowable across every era.
rows.anchor: وبناه للمفعول تعظيما للأأمر بالإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun focuses the question on each person’s particular sin; the virtuous are questioned about good deeds to honor them and admonish those below.
rows.anchor: وقد سئل المحسن عن حسنته سؤال تشريف له وتنديم لمن دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are named first because they are the main focus, their messenger was human, and familiar witnessed examples teach most clearly; jinn are added to show all are easy for God.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنس أعظم مقصود بهذا , ولهذا كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents the distinction between criminals and obedient people as a favor, preventing confusion from frightening or reproaching the obedient.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا التمييز من أجل النعم لئلا يؤدي الالتباس إلى ترويع بعض المطيعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain asks whether listeners deny the Lord’s nurturing favors, including the sense of smell from the front or other gifts.
rows.anchor: أبنعمة الشم من الأمام أم من غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the wording is general, the context specifies recognizing criminals, rather than questioning them about sins or other matters.
rows.anchor: الكلام عاما عرف انه خاص بتعرف المجرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sins, once hidden, become legible in signs such as blue eyes, black faces, blindness, deafness, and walking on their faces.
rows.anchor: زرقة العيون وسواد الوجوه والعمى والصمم والمشي على الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are also recognized by luminous white faces, smiling, and signs such as the ghurra and taḥjīl.
rows.anchor: وكما يعرف المحسنون بسيماهم من بياض الوجوه وإشراقها وتبسمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forelocks are the fronts of the heads; passive wording makes the criminals’ seizure seem effortless, by any captor appointed for it.
rows.anchor: إلى سهولة الأخذ من أي آخذ كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their forelocks and feet are joined, then they are dragged helplessly by whoever God appoints and cast into the Fire; this reverses their habit of joining what God separated and separating what He joined.
rows.anchor: ما أمر الله به أن يفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The just punishment is framed as a favor: everyone disowns criminality and wishes severe retribution for criminals, while each person receives what their worldly deeds merit.
rows.anchor: لأن كل أحد ينتفي من الإجرام ويود للمجرمين عظيم الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seizure leads to a humiliating destination: the great, ugly pit of Hell, described as near and clinging close to the hearers.
rows.anchor: أي الحفرة العظيمة الكريهة المنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Raḥmān classified criminals, forerunners, and followers and closed with retribution and honor, this sūra unfolds their afterlife conditions.
rows.anchor: لما صنف سبحانه الناس في تلك إلى ثلاث أصناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa is the second blast, bringing the universal resurrection and assembly of all creatures for judgment under God’s manifest, unshared rule.
rows.anchor: وهي النفخة الثانية التي يكون عنها البعث الأكبر الذي هو القيامة الجامعة لجميع الخلق للحكم بينهم على الانفراد الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article signals perfection: no event deserves the complete name “the Occurrence” as fully as the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولا واقع يستحق أن يسمى الواقعة بلام الكمال وتاء المبالغة غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional “when” may be attached to an omitted predicate, leaving the mind to imagine the awe-inspiring events that follow.
rows.anchor: منصوبا بالمحذوف لتذهب النفس فيه كل مذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its occurrence is utterly certain: nothing in its circumstances can be called false, and no falsehood will prevail there; every promised event arrives and every denied event remains absent.
rows.anchor: بل كل ما أخبر بمجيئه جاء من غير أن يرده شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lowers whom He wills among the Fire’s eminent inhabitants and raises the weak among Paradise’s people to the highest ranks; none can overturn His judgment.
rows.anchor: لا راد لأمره ولا معقب لحكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowering and raising may affect the people of the Fire and Paradise, and also mountains and other things as God wills.
rows.anchor: من عظماء أهل النار وغيرهم مما يشاؤه من الجبال وغيرها إلى أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entire broad earth is violently shaken, first rising and falling and then convulsing intensely, all by the slightest divine command.
rows.anchor: زلزلت زلزالا شديدا بعنف فانخفضت ارتفعت

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī gives the lexical sense of rajj as movement or shaking.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : والرج في اللغة التحريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are pulverized and their stone mixes with soil, becoming like fluffed wool and moving like clouds.
rows.anchor: فتتت على صلابتها وعظمها بأدنى إشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pulverized mountains become particles scattered on their own, needing no wind, like dust visible in a sunbeam.
rows.anchor: أي منتشرا متفرقا بنفسه من غير حاجة إلى هواء يفرقه فهو كالذي يرى في شعاع الشمس إذا دخل في كوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are divided according to their worldly dispositions into three classes, each with a higher and lower rank, displaying the completeness of divine power.
rows.anchor: أي قسمتم بما كان في جبلاتكم وطباعكم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī explains that a class is called a pair when it is or is mentioned with another half.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي : وكل صنف يكون أو يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the right are associated with the right direction, its place, and its deeds; they include both forerunners and later righteous believers.
rows.anchor: أي جهة اليمين وموضعها وأعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated construction makes the second phrase a new subject and a predicate for the first, with the repeated subject serving as the link.
rows.anchor: والجملة خبر عن الأولى , والرابط تكرار المبتدأ بلفظه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān observes that this kind of repetition most often conveys awe and magnification.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان رحمه الله تعالى : وأكثر ما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question magnifies the right-hand people as so blessed that their condition merits inquiry.
rows.anchor: ثم فخم أمرهم بالتعجيب من حالهم بقوله منبها على أنهم أهل لأن يسأل عنهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the two preceding sūras presented decisive proofs, while the close of al-Qamar taught that every worldly event occurs by God’s decree.
rows.anchor: أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تقدم الإعذار في السورتين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the close of al-Qamar’s decree teaching to its cited verses, then says al-Wāqiʿa opens by making the afterlife division explicit.
rows.anchor: وأعلمهم سبحانه في الواقعة بانقسامهم الأخروي فافتتح ذكر الساعة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: He contrasts this sūra’s full, explicit account of afterlife states with the earlier sūras’ worldly instruction and subtler allusions; its ending confirms the final recompense.
rows.anchor: فتجردت هذه السورة للتعريف بأحوالهم الأخروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the left are associated with the direction, place, and deeds of ill fortune.
rows.anchor: أي جهة الشؤم وموضعها وأعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question heightens the gravity of their fate and the wonder of the evil that reached them despite their sound faculties.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أهل لأن يسأل عما أصابهم من الشؤم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing both sides, the author highlights the highest rank among the right-hand people to encourage excellence, while leaving the left undivided to warn of its end.
rows.anchor: ذكر أعلى أهل القسم الأول ترغيبا في أحسن حالهم ولم يقسم أهل المشأمة ترهيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forerunners race to obedience; they belong to the first two gardens mentioned in al-Raḥmān and are the people of the heart, uniquely deserving the higher station.
rows.anchor: إلى أعمال الطاعة أصحاب الجنتين الأوليين في الرحمن وهم أصحاب القلب

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī attributes to the Prophet a description of forerunners as those who accept a right when given, give when asked, and judge others as themselves.
rows.anchor: وعن المهدوي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose and brought them near; without His act of drawing them close, they would not have become forerunners.
rows.anchor: الذين اصطفاهم الله تعالى للسبق فأرادهم لقربه أو أنعم عليهم بقربه

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī describes the close as freed from self-interest: all religious and worldly deeds and both divine and human rights are treated as God’s rights; he distinguishes those absorbed in awe from those entrusted with easier service.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : المقربون تخلصوا من نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their gardens contain the only complete bliss, untroubled by any distress or interruption.
rows.anchor: أي الذي لا نعيم غيره لأنه لا كدر فيه بوجه ولا منغص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thullah means a large, fine gathering; al-Baghawī glosses it as a group whose number is not bounded.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي : والثلة جماعة غير محصورة العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier multitude comprises past prophets and those who believed them without an intermediary.
rows.anchor: وهم الأنبياء الماضون عليهم الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later few are those who believed Muhammad, counted here at about 120,000; the 600,000 fighting men who followed Moses imply still larger total populations.
rows.anchor: عليه الصلاة والسلام مائة ألف ونيفا وعشرين ألفا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says both the large group and the few are from this community; al-Ṭabarānī and Ibn ʿAdī transmit it through Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, whom the author calls abandoned.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما , وفيه أبان بن أبي عياش وهو متروك

rows.speaker: أبو بكرة
rows.claim: A report from Abū Bakra comes both as Prophetic and stopped at him, through weak ʿAlī ibn Zayd; the author says the stopped version is sounder and that either applies correctly to this community.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكرة رضي الله عنه مرفوعا وموقوفا , والموقوف أولى بالصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applying both groups to this community, the author counts the Companions and righteous followers through the start of the third century among the great group, before Islam’s later decline.
rows.anchor: فتكون الصحابة رضي الله عنهم كلهم من هذه الثلة وكذا من تبعهم بإحسان إلى رأس القرن الثالث

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The author invokes the Prophetic report that Islam began as a stranger and will become a stranger again, with glad tidings for the strangers.
rows.anchor: بدأ الإسلام غريبا وسيكون غريبا فطوبى للغرباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows an alternative: a great group of doomed deniers from earlier nations and a few deniers from the later community.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يقدر أيضا : وثلة - أي جماعة كثيرة هلكى - من الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage explains earlier nations’ destruction and deliverance as God's act, then identifies the rejection of messengers as the cause.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر ما أحله بهم سبحانه وأشار إلى القطع بأنه من عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the great calamity, which decisively shows that disbelief is utterly false and angers the Creator.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر الشنيع العظيم من الوبال الدال قطعا على أن الكفر أبطل الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike Ghāfir, this sūra does not aim to classify people into two groups; classification appears incidentally to establish the Hour, so the pronoun of the matter is enough.
rows.anchor: ولما لم يكن مقصودها كمقصود غافر من تصنيف الناس صنفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers came to their own peoples habitually, chosen by God to bring them clear proofs, including scriptures that unmistakably establish their mission and make the punishment more severe.
rows.anchor: أي رسل الله الذين أرسلهم إليهم وخصهم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human dignity is rightly asserted against rebellious devils but wrongly becomes pride against God’s friends; the disbelievers misplaced their self-regard.
rows.anchor: فمن وضعها موضعها بالتكبر على من أمر الله بالتكبر عليه وهم شياطين الإنس والجن ممن عصاه سبحانه نجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar is a generic human category and is nominative as the agent because the interrogative calls for a verb.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الجنس وهو مرفوع على الفاعلية لأن الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural verb preserves the collective force of the messengers’ rejection; a singular would lose the awe of their combined denial.
rows.anchor: وكان لو أفرد الضمير لم يكن له روعة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disbelieved immediately and without reflection, out of envy that human messengers equal them in humanity and received a special commission.
rows.anchor: بذلك عقب مجيء الرسل وبسببه من غير نظر وتفكر وأدنى تأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reasoned that God’s greatness required nonhuman messengers, but reflection would show that ordinary people could not bear seeing angels; prophets receive added capacity, and humans are more receptive to their own kind.
rows.anchor: وهم الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام بقوى زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers serve creatures’ interests, not God’s; when people turn away, God leaves them to their choice, harming only themselves.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا كله إنما هو لمصالح الخلق لا يعود على الله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has always been independent of all creation and eternally possesses complete perfection and praise; nothing newly accrues to Him.
rows.anchor: له صفة الغنى المطلق والحمد الأبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having established belief in God, messengers, scriptures, and providence, the passage identifies denial of resurrection as the chief motive for disbelief.
rows.anchor: ولما قرر وجوب الإيمان به وبرسله وكتبه وبالقدر خيره وشره

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar calls zaʿama a euphemism for lying.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : هي كنية الكذب

rows.speaker: أبو مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Abū Masʿūd in Abū Dāwūd says that “they claim” is a bad mount for a man.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أبي مسعود رضي الله عنه عند أبي داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb signals a claim of knowledge without proof: the disbelievers sound certain while remaining doubtful and, in reality, false.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم شاكون وإن كانوا جازمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers covered the evidence for God’s oneness, even though reason points to it.
rows.anchor: أي أوقعوا الستر لما دلت عليه العقول من وحدانية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim denies that any agent will resurrect them in any way.
rows.anchor: أي من باعث ما بوجه من الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands a direct “yes,” then reinforces it with an oath by the Lord who aided the Prophet through vindicating truth and overturning falsehood.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إلي بالانتقام ممن كذب بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive form presents resurrection as their unavoidable subjection to force, accomplished by God with ease.
rows.anchor: مشيرا ببنائه للمفعول إلى أنه ويكون على وجه القهر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will certainly receive a grave report of their deeds from whoever God appoints; resurrection and accounting are easy for God because all possible things stand equally within His power.
rows.anchor: أي لتخبرن حتما إخبارا عظيما ممن يقيمه الله لإخباركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra urges considered conduct and religious manners with God, the Messenger, and other people, especially gracious treatment of women following the Prophet’s exemplary companionship.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الحث على تقدير التدبير في الأدب مع الله ومع رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومع سائر العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proper religious etiquette may call for gentleness and patience, for a disciplinary blow, or for the sword, according to what the situation requires.
rows.anchor: باللين والأناة ، وأخرى بالسوط وما داناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra’s names, al-Taḥrīm and al-Nabī, each point to the conduct and etiquette it explains.
rows.anchor: وكل من اسميها التحريم والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم موضح لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala praises God’s perpetual perfection, His broad generosity to all servants, and His completion of Islam’s blessing for those especially favored.
rows.anchor: الذي أتم خواصه نعمة الإسلام
